candidates.statement: Observe that it will suffice to choose $Q_{j_2} \in \mathop{\mathrm{SL}}(2,\mathbb{C})$ such that $$\label{radadadadadadada} \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\left( X_{{j_3}+1}\cdots X_n X_1\cdots X_{j_1} \cdots Q_{j_2}X_{j_2}Q_{j_2}^{-1}\cdots X_{j_{3}-1} \right) =2 \cos\left( \frac{2\pi l_{j_3}}{p_{j_3}}\right)$$ because this will ensure that there exists some $Q_{j_3} \in \mathop{\mathrm{SL}}(2,\mathbb{C})$ with the property that $$Q_{j_3} X_{{j_3}+1}\cdots X_n X_1\cdots X_{j_1} \cdots Q_{j_2}X_{j_2}Q_{j_2}^{-1}\cdots X_{j_{3}-1} Q_{j_3}^{-1}=X_{j_3},$$ since non-diagonalizable elements of $\mathop{\mathrm{SL}}(2,\mathbb{C})$ have trace $\pm2$, given that the unit determinant condition implies that the unique eigenvalue with multiplicity two for such elements must be either $1$ or $-1$ and we have that $$2 \left|\cos\left( \frac{2\pi l_{j_3}}{p_{j_3}}\right) \right|<2.$$ For [\[radadadadadadada\]](#radadadadadadada){reference-type="eqref" reference="radadadadadadada"} we used our assumption on $j_3.$ Write $$\begin{aligned} &X_{{j_3}+1}\cdots X_n X_1\cdots X_{j_1} \cdots X_{j_2-1}=\exp(ia), \\ &X_{j_2}=\exp(ib), \\ &X_{j_2+1} \cdots X_{j_{3}-1}=\exp(ic), \\ &X_{j_3} =\exp(id). \end{aligned}$

candidates.statement: Assume $uz-vw=1$ so that $\tilde Q\in \mathop{\mathrm{SL}}(2,\mathbb{C}).$ We compute $$\begin{gathered} X_{{j_3}+1}\cdots X_n X_1\cdots X_{j_1} \cdots X_{j_2-1} \tilde QX_{j_2} \tilde Q^{-1} X_{j_2+1}\cdots X_{j_{3}-1} \\ = \begin{pmatrix} zue^{i(a+b+c)}-wve^{i(a-b+c)} & -uve^{i(a+b-c)}+uve^{i(a-b-c)} \\ zve^{i(b+c-a)}-zwe^{i(c-a-b)} & -vwe^{-i(a+b+c)}+zue^{i(b-a-c)} \end{pmatrix}. \end{gathered}$$ Thus we have that $$\begin{gathered} \text{tr}\begin{pmatrix} zue^{i(a+b+c)}-wve^{i(a-b+c)} & -uve^{i(a+b-c)}+uve^{i(a-b-c)} \\ zwe^{i(b+c-a)}-zwe^{i(c-a-b)} & -vwe^{-i(a+b+c)}+zue^{i(b-a-c)} \end{pmatrix}\\ =2zu\cos(a+b+c)-2wv\cos(a+c-b). \end{gathered}$$ It follows that we must solve $$\label{system} \begin{pmatrix} \cos(a+b+c) & \cos(a+c-b) \\ 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} zu \\ -wv \end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix} 2\cos(d) \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}.$$ Using the trigonometric identity $\cos(x+y) - \cos(x-y)=-2\sin(x)\sin(y)$ we get $$\begin{aligned} \det \begin{pmatrix} \cos(a+b+c) & \cos(a+c-b) \\ 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix}&= \cos((a+c)+b)-\cos((a+c)-b) \\ &=-2\sin(a+c)\sin(b).

candidates.statement: ::: proof *Proof.* It is clear that $\mathop{\mathrm{CS}}_{\mathbb{C}}^*(X) \subset \mathcal{W}(p_1,...,p_n).$ We must show that for any $y \in \mathbb{Z}$ which is not divisible by more than three of the $p_j$ we can find $l=(l_1,...,l_n) \in L(p_1,...,p_n)$ which solves the congruence equation $$\label{congruence} y^2 = \left(P\left( \frac{l_1}{p_1}+\sum_{j=2}^{n} \frac{2 l_j}{p_j}\right) \right)^2 \ \mathop{\mathrm{mod}}\ 4P\mathbb{Z}$$ For $x \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $d \in \mathbb{N}$ let $[x]_d$ denote the congruence class of $x$ in the quotient ring $\mathbb{Z} / d\mathbb{Z}.$ Since $p_j$ is odd for $j\geq 2,$ it follows that $4p_1,p_2,...,p_n$ are also pairwise co-prime.
